description: The workbench page is a remote origin (http://127.0.0.1:<kernel port>), so Tauri's ACL denies its invokes by default. Grant only what the workbench page actually calls: the injected harness scripts; the browser half of an embedded builtin plugin (plugins/memory/client/client.js calls memory_recent_injections for the session-header badge — titles and ids only, never a memory body — and a missing grant there degrades to a silently absent badge rather than an error, so it is pinned by that plugin's own test instead of by the harness-invoke judgment, which scans the injected harness scripts (harness/harness-draft.js, harness/harness-health.js, harness/context-menu-fallback.js, harness/workbench-appearance.js)); allow-window-appearance is the appearance mirror: workbench-appearance.js forwards the kernel's declared ui-theme preference (`html[data-ds-theme-source]`) to set_window_appearance, which touches only the harness window's native appearance. `system` forwards null (no override), so the page's own prefers-color-scheme query stays live — pinning it is what killed the kernel's「跟随系统」until 2026-10-18. A misconfigured grant degrades to a light/dark titlebar over the opposite page palette, never to a broken page; plus one caller nobody writes in this repo: tauri-plugin-opener injects its own click interceptor (init-iife.js, open_js_links_on_click defaults to true) into EVERY webview, and it calls plugin:opener|open_url on any `<a target="_blank">` / Ctrl-click without a .catch (2026-10-15: the kernel renders conversation links exactly that way, so one click produced an unhandled rejection, harness-health.js reported it as a workbench fault, and guard.rs then mis-attributed it to the kernel). `opener:allow-default-urls` is required alongside `opener:allow-open-url` because that command validates the URL scope itself (tauri-plugin-opener src/commands.rs): granting the command alone turns the ACL refusal into a ForbiddenUrl error — the same denial in different words. `opener:default` is deliberately NOT used: it would also bring allow-reveal-item-in-dir, which the workbench page has no use for. It is not a no-op either: on_new_window only hands http(s) to the system browser and denies every other scheme, while the interceptor preventDefaults those same four protocols and calls the command itself, so before this grant a `target="_blank"` link never reached on_new_window at all. Net effect: http(s) links now open (that was the bug), and mailto:/tel: reach the OS handler too — both click-gated, no worse than the user clicking the link themselves. The wildcard port covers the release/debug defaults (3090/3091) and any custom port in settings.json; the origin is still pinned to loopback and the harness window.
